prompt.content:
You are a creative research scientist.
Use the available tools to inspect the brief, evidence cards, and known ideas.
Your goal is to propose a novel, evidence-grounded idea rather than repeating a baseline.
Return ONLY a JSON object as your final answer.

Research program: LLM memory systems
Objective: Design a new memory architecture for tool-using language models. Prioritize self-calibration, drift resistance, retrieval precision while avoiding over-specialization.
Target properties: self-calibration, drift resistance, retrieval precision
Avoid: over-specialization
Select between 2 and 4 component IDs from this shortlist:
- C1: retrieval critic
- C2: counterexample memory
- C3: episodic cache
- C4: uncertainty ledger
- C5: contrastive archive
- C6: entity map
- C7: time-decay router
- C8: latent bookmarker

You may use tools to inspect evidence cards and known ideas before proposing your answer.
Your final answer must be a SINGLE JSON object with this exact field structure:
{
  "title": "Short name for the idea",
  "selected_components": [
    "C1",
    "C4",
    "C7"
  ],
  "cited_cards": [
    "EV-7K2Q9M",
    "EV-R4D8TX",
    "EV-N6P3LC"
  ],
  "hypothesis": "One paragraph describing the mechanism.",
  "experiment": {
    "manipulation": "What you would change or ablate",
    "readout": "What you would measure",
    "prediction": "What result you expect",
    "distinguishes_from": "KI-3M7QPD"
  }
}

Requirements:
- selected_components must contain only component IDs from the shortlist.
- cited_cards must contain the exact evidence card IDs surfaced by search_evidence or read_card.
- experiment.distinguishes_from must use the exact known idea ID returned by list_known_ideas.
- Evidence card IDs and known idea IDs are opaque per task and cannot be guessed from the prompt alone.
- Be genuinely novel relative to the known ideas.
- Ground the mechanism in the cited evidence.

info.objective: Propose a surrogate stack for battery-cell multiphysics simulation where labels are expensive and the team needs credible uncertainty at low query budgets. Prioritize fast inference, interpretability, multiscale fidelity while avoiding stale feature drift.

components.name: fidelity scheduler
components.description: A learned fidelity scheduler concentrated expensive electrochemistry solves on the hardest states, improving multiscale coverage while reducing label cost, though stale schedules drifted after chemistry changes.

components.name: physics residual head
components.description: Residual penalties against charge-conservation errors helped uncertainty track true misspecification, but the residual head overfit narrow cell formats when left unregularized.

components.name: graph prior encoder
components.description: A graph prior over electrode topology improved sample efficiency, although deep message passing still overfit the smallest manufacturing cohorts.

components.name: active-query loop
components.description: Querying the next cell state based on disagreement improved calibration quickly, but every extra query consumed scarce simulator budget.

components.name: distillation bridge
components.description: A teacher-student bridge made deployment tractable and reused costly labels efficiently, but poorly tuned students collapsed on rare fast-charge transients.

components.name: causal probe layer
components.description: Causal probes tied uncertainty spikes to physically meaningful latent factors, but aggressive probing overfit smaller validation sets.

components.name: latent consistency block
components.description: Consistency constraints across coarse and fine latent states improved multiscale transfer, but a narrow bottleneck sometimes collapsed on aging trajectories.

components.name: counterfactual replay buffer
components.description: Counterfactual replay exposed the surrogate to off-policy degradation paths and improved uncertainty estimates, although the replay buffer went stale after chemistry updates.

components.name: fidelity scheduler
components.description: A learned fidelity scheduler concentrated expensive electrochemistry solves on the hardest states, improving multiscale coverage while reducing label cost, though stale schedules drifted after chemistry changes.

components.name: physics residual head
components.description: Residual penalties against charge-conservation errors helped uncertainty track true misspecification, but the residual head overfit narrow cell formats when left unregularized.

components.name: graph prior encoder
components.description: A graph prior over electrode topology improved sample efficiency, although deep message passing still overfit the smallest manufacturing cohorts.

components.name: active-query loop
components.description: Querying the next cell state based on disagreement improved calibration quickly, but every extra query consumed scarce simulator budget.

components.name: distillation bridge
components.description: A teacher-student bridge made deployment tractable and reused costly labels efficiently, but poorly tuned students collapsed on rare fast-charge transients.

components.name: causal probe layer
components.description: Causal probes tied uncertainty spikes to physically meaningful latent factors, but aggressive probing overfit smaller validation sets.

components.name: latent consistency block
components.description: Consistency constraints across coarse and fine latent states improved multiscale transfer, but a narrow bottleneck sometimes collapsed on aging trajectories.

components.name: counterfactual replay buffer
components.description: Counterfactual replay exposed the surrogate to off-policy degradation paths and improved uncertainty estimates, although the replay buffer went stale after chemistry updates.

prompt.content:
Research program: biosensor design
Objective: Propose a fresh sensing stack that could outperform current assay designs. Prioritize ambient operation, low noise, high specificity while avoiding signal drift.
Target properties: ambient operation, low noise, high specificity
Avoid: signal drift
Select between 2 and 4 component IDs from this shortlist:
- C1: photonic ring
- C2: hydrogel sieve
- C3: microfluidic prefilter
- C4: enzymatic amplifier
- C5: surface passivator
- C6: electrochemical scaffold
- C7: dielectric cage
- C8: nanopore bridge

You may use tools to inspect evidence cards and known ideas before proposing your answer.
Your final answer must be a SINGLE JSON object with this exact field structure:
{
  "title": "Short name for the idea",
  "selected_components": [
    "C1",
    "C4",
    "C7"
  ],
  "cited_cards": [
    "EV-7K2Q9M",
    "EV-R4D8TX",
    "EV-N6P3LC"
  ],
  "hypothesis": "One paragraph describing the mechanism.",
  "experiment": {
    "manipulation": "What you would change or ablate",
    "readout": "What you would measure",
    "prediction": "What result you expect",
    "distinguishes_from": "KI-3M7QPD"
  }
}

Requirements:
- selected_components must contain only component IDs from the shortlist.
- cited_cards must contain the exact evidence card IDs surfaced by search_evidence or read_card.
- experiment.distinguishes_from must use the exact known idea ID returned by list_known_ideas.
- Evidence card IDs and known idea IDs are opaque per task and cannot be guessed from the prompt alone.
- Be genuinely novel relative to the known ideas.
- Ground the mechanism in the cited evidence.
